title: Omega-3 and DHA in Pregnancy: Food Sources and Supplement Cautions
excerpt: Why DHA matters for fetal development, low-mercury fish options, and when to ask a clinician about supplements
content:
## Introduction to Omega-3 and DHA
Omega-3 and DHA are two types of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) that are crucial for the health of both mother and fetus. DHA (Docosahexaenoic acid) is a particular type of omega-3 fatty acid that is essential for the development of the fetus's brain and vision.

## The Role of DHA in Pregnancy
DHA plays a critical role in the development of the fetus's brain and vision. It also supports the development of the nervous system and cardiovascular system. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), DHA is one of the most important nutrients for fetal development.

## Food Sources of Omega-3 and DHA
There are many food sources that are rich in Omega-3 and DHA, including:
* Fatty fish like salmon, sardines, and mackerel
* Shellfish like oysters and mussels
* Fortified foods like eggs and yogurt
* Plant-based sources like flaxseeds, chia seeds, and walnuts

## Precautions When Eating Fish During Pregnancy
While fish is a rich source of Omega-3 and DHA, pregnant women need to be cautious when eating fish during pregnancy. Fish can contain mercury, a toxic substance that can harm fetal development. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), pregnant women should limit their consumption of high-mercury fish like shark, swordfish, and king mackerel.

## Omega-3 and DHA Supplements
Omega-3 and DHA supplements can be an option for pregnant women who are not getting enough of these nutrients from their diet. However, pregnant women should consult with their healthcare provider before taking any supplements to ensure safety and efficacy.

## Conclusion
Omega-3 and DHA are two types of polyunsaturated fatty acids that are crucial for the health of both mother and fetus. Pregnant women should consume enough food sources rich in Omega-3 and DHA, limit their consumption of high-mercury fish, and consult with their healthcare provider before taking any supplements.

## Important Note
Before taking any supplements, pregnant women should consult with their healthcare provider to ensure safety and efficacy. For more information on prenatal nutrition and pregnancy meal planning, visit our [website](/blog) or [read more about this topic](/blog/topics).
